papers.title: DeliMF: Gated Cross-Attention Fusion of Structured Time Series and Clinical Text for Early Intensive Care Delirium Prediction
papers.abstract: Delirium affects a large fraction of intensive care unit (ICU) patients and foreshadows longer stays, lasting cognitive decline, and higher mortality. Flagging the patients who will become delirious within the first day of admission would give clinicians a window to intervene. Yet state-of-the-art predictors rely only on the structured electronic health record (EHR) of vital signs, laboratory values, and medications, while overlooking the free-text clinical notes written in the same window, which carry information the numbers cannot encode. To this end, we present DeliMF, a multimodal framework that fuses the structured time series with clinical text. It encodes the structured signals with a temporal Transformer and the time-stamped radiology reports with a clinical text encoder, and fuses the two through a gated cross-attention module. The gate learns a per-patient weight on the text; when a patient has no note the gate closes and DeliMF reduces to its structured-only form, giving robustness to missing text by construction. On an incident-only MIMIC-IV cohort, DeliMF improves significantly over the baselines, particularly on patients who carry clinical text, while losing nothing on those without. Ablation studies confirm the contribution of multimodal fusion and gated cross-attention, and a case study further shows that fusing clinical text with the structured stream recovers delirium cases that the structured data alone misses. We hope DeliMF encourages early ICU prediction to make fuller use of the overlooked clinical text and contributes to the early identification and timely intervention of delirium.

papers.title: Conditional Weight of Evidence for Gradient-Boosted Credit Models: Estimation, Additivity and Its Relation to Adverse Action Reasons
papers.abstract: Traditional weight of evidence assigns a credit characteristic a value based on its association with default across a population. Credit analysis also requires an assessment of that characteristic in the context of an individual applicant's record. We study conditional weight of evidence for this purpose. It measures the change in default log odds from observing a characteristic after the remaining credit information is known. Its sign identifies whether the characteristic adds adverse or favorable information for that applicant, and its magnitude measures the strength of that information. The same characteristic value can therefore receive different assessments for applicants with different payment histories or other credit attributes. We develop estimators using gradient-boosted trees and evaluate their accuracy in a bureau-style simulation. Regressions of the full model's predicted probabilities recover conditional evidence more accurately than separate models fitted to default outcomes, provided the full model is accurate. They also recover a deliberately constructed file-age effect whose direction varies with utilization and is often missed by marginal weight of evidence. Local class-frequency estimates improve on marginal weight of evidence but remain inaccurate for some weak effects. An application to FICO HELOC data illustrates estimation when the population evidence is unknown. Conditional weight of evidence provides an applicant-specific interpretation of the information in a credit characteristic; its population summary, a conditional information value, splits the joint information in the record across blocks when averaged over orderings. Neither is an adverse action reason, which explains the fitted score difference between the applicant and chosen passing records.

papers.title: LIBERO-Pro2.0: A Benchmark for Evaluating the Robustness of Embodied Foundation Models
papers.abstract: LIBERO has emerged as a widely adopted benchmark for evaluating robotic manipulation policies. However, strong performance on LIBERO does not necessarily indicate robust embodied capabilities, as models may exploit benchmark-specific regularities rather than generalize to diverse operating conditions. In this work, we introduce LIBERO-Pro2.0, a comprehensive benchmark for systematically evaluating the robustness of embodied foundation models under distribution shifts. LIBERO-Pro2.0 encompasses 22 static perturbations and 20 runtime interventions across six dimensions: Condition, Environment, Observation, Execution, Robot State Configuration, and Language, yielding 1,648 validated shifted task instances. To support robustness-oriented learning, we further collect 39,390 training trajectories through model-generated and human demonstrations. All shifted task instances undergo six rounds of iterative human review and correction to ensure physical plausibility and task validity. We evaluate 17 representative robot policies spanning vision-language-action models, world-action models, and robustness-oriented policies. Our results reveal substantial robustness gaps across all evaluated paradigms: under runtime distribution shifts, the evaluated models exhibit an average performance drop of 26.5 percentage points, with individual drops reaching 32.5 points. These findings highlight the gap between nominal benchmark performance and robustness under distribution shifts, underscoring the need for systematic robustness evaluation of embodied foundation models.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Koopman Learning for Data-Efficient System Identification of Automated Vehicle Dynamics
papers.abstract: Understanding how a particular automated vehicle reacts to nearby traffic can improve motion prediction, control development, traffic simulation, and safety evaluation. However, commercial automated driving systems are proprietary, and single encounters may provide only a few seconds of noisy data. Standard physical models are interpretable but inflexible, whereas neural models are often data-hungry. We propose a physics-informed Koopman framework that combines a calibrated car-following law with a correction learned from the observations. A weak-form estimator learns this correction from velocity measurements integrated over time, avoiding noise-sensitive numerical differentiation. The resulting continuous-time model predicts the follower's response and provides interpretable measures of driving behavior. Experiments on OpenACC and CATS-CF evaluate 5-, 7-, and 11-second histories. Averaged over these histories, the constant-time-headway branch reduces speed prediction error by 16.0% and 15.4% on OpenACC and CATS-CF, respectively, relative to the best neural baselines. The PI-Koopman branches achieve the lowest mean speed and gap errors among the physical and neural comparators. Weak-form estimation reduces acceleration-field reconstruction error by 74.5% in noisy known-law simulations and noise-induced field perturbation by 91.6% in paired real-vehicle measurements. The same PI-Koopman system identification supports following-mode recognition with an approximately eleven-fold difference in median residual variance between human drivers and automated vehicles, and a single residual threshold achieves 85.4% balanced accuracy. The branch informed by the intelligent driver model takes a median 17 to 26 ms for identification and forecasting on the tested central processing units, supporting frequent target adaptation.

papers.title: Autonomous Thermal Switching Outperforms the Frozen Optimum with Vanishing Correlations
papers.abstract: Can autonomous thermal switching outperform the best frozen barrier allocation while keeping system--auxiliary correlations arbitrarily small? We establish this relaxation advantage at fixed lowering budget and visible equilibrium, preserving joint detailed balance. On finite reversible networks, optimal fast switching mixes profiles concentrating the budget on single edges. A three-state model gives a strict gain and its finite-rate threshold. Faster switching preserves the gain while correlations vanish throughout relaxation. Collective and continuous models suggest a colloidal test.

papers.title: Scene-Adaptive VLA: Efficient Autonomous Driving via Dynamic Layer Routing
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models offer a promising paradigm for autonomous driving. However, the massive parameter scale of VLAs strains onboard computational resources during real-time inference. This directly increases energy consumption and limits vehicle battery range, making it critical to minimize computational overhead without compromising driving capability and explainability. Current research on efficient VLA-based driving focuses on sequential adaptation (\textit{e.g.}, Chain-of-Thought and token adjustment), leaving structural adaptation underexplored despite parameter redundancy across dynamic driving scenes. To address this gap, we propose Scene-Adaptive VLA, an efficient framework leveraging dynamic layer routing to adjust active parameters based on real-time scenes. Inspired by the temporal continuity of scenes and model predictive uncertainty, our approach characterizes model-perceived scene complexity via frame-level temporal scene variations and decision deviations. To uncover latent scene-to-parameter correspondences, we encode this characterization into scene-aware tokens, alongside two specialized queries. A budget-conditioned layer routing mechanism evaluates these refined queries to allocate a budget that determines the active parameter ratio and subsequently selects appropriate layer combinations. The entire framework is optimized end-to-end. Extensive evaluations on the Bench2Drive benchmark show that when adapted to a state-of-the-art VLA model, our approach significantly reduces inference-time computational overhead by 53.5\% with negligible degradation in driving and language capabilities. Code is available at https:github.com/yang-luvu/Scene-Adaptive-VLA.

papers.title: Score-optimized copula coupling for multivariate ensemble post-processing
papers.abstract: Statistical post-processing can calibrate the individual components of an ensemble forecast but may also distort relationships between forecast dimensions. This paper proposes Score-Optimized Copula Coupling, which rearranges calibrated forecast samples according to an optimized dependence structure to restore potentially lost dependencies. We assess fixed and adaptively updated versions using wind-speed and temperature forecasts. In the variable-specific spatial case studies, all versions significantly outperform the strongest benchmarks, with improvements of 1.08-2.02 percent in energy score and 5.45-7.97 percent in variogram score. A third case study at 24 co-located stations shows that one optimized structure can represent both spatial and inter-variable relationships. The largest energy and variogram score improvements are 3.98 and 3.69 percent for spatial dependence and 1.16 and 1.06 percent for inter-variable dependence; all are statistically significant. Additional calibration terms improve covariance representation but can reduce gains in the other scores.

papers.title: Local quadratic convergence of iterated correlation matrices: bounds and counterexamples
papers.abstract: Kruskal's unpublished manuscript on CONCOR gives a local argument for convergence of successive correlations to a prescribed two-class sign pattern. We identify a failure in its stated one-step estimate and establish a replacement bound for correlation matrices in arbitrary dimension. A geometric estimate for sign-aligned centered rows yields an explicit sufficient neighbourhood of convergence and a quadratic error bound. We construct invariant families of correlation matrices with an exact scalar recurrence in every dimension at least three. These families yield counterexamples to the original estimate in every dimension at least four. The failure persists on relatively open sets of positive-definite correlation matrices. In dimensions divisible by four, an explicitly solvable subfamily provides counterexamples arbitrarily close to the prescribed fixed point and attains the asymptotic coefficient in the new bound. Quadratic order is attained by the constructed families in every dimension at least three. These counterexamples concern the quantitative estimate, not the convergence conclusion: all the exhibited trajectories converge to their prescribed sign patterns.

papers.title: Training with Ciphers to Enhance In-Context Terminology Learning For Translation from Rare Languages
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning LLMs with in-context examples (IC-Train) lets translation models adapt to new parallel data at deployment, but it is unclear whether they actually learn the translations of rare terms from those examples. We formalize this capability as in-context term learning (ICTL). We show that standard IC-Train develops this capability only weakly, and propose RareCipherFT, which strengthens it without any lexical resources. RareCipherFT pairs each training target with in-context examples that share a rare term with it. It then replaces that term with a character-shuffled cipher in both the context and the reference, so the term can only be recovered by copying from context. The ciphered fraction of training data is annealed to preserve translation quality. Across seven translation directions between English and Tamil, Assamese, Mizo, Nepali and Hausa, and four models from 1B to 7B parameters, RareCipherFT raises term recall over standard IC-Train by 5-15 absolute points without lowering COMET. Probes using synonyms, nonce words and controls for shared surface context show that these gains come from linking source terms to their in-context translations rather than from shortcuts.

papers.title: Casimir multiplets suffice: strong generation in $\mathcal{N}=4$ $SU(N)$ SYM
papers.abstract: The Schur sector of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang$--$Mills theory contains infinitely many protected operators, while the invariant polynomials of a single adjoint scalar are organized by finitely many Casimir degrees. I prove that the small $\mathcal N=4$ short multiplets built from these invariants strongly generate the associated chiral algebra, thereby establishing the $SU(N)$ case of the strong-generation conjecture of Beem et al. For every $N\ge2$, all field components associated with degrees $2,\ldots,N$ suffice, in every conformal weight and every degree of the standard relative quantum BRST cohomology. The proof brings together cyclic trace cohomology, quantum lifting, and an arbitrary-degree quartic$--$odd transport identity. Exact field relations and a finite-rank Newton obstruction exclude every additional lowest space, including non-scalar flavor representations; the required normal-ordering corrections and BRST primitives are derived explicitly. The resulting completeness theorem explains how a finite family of supersymmetric multiplets organizes an unbounded quantum spectrum. Every Schur class is a normal polynomial in their components and derivatives, even when its gauge-theory representative involves fermions and arbitrarily many derivatives. This supplies a uniform set of local inputs for meromorphic operator products, bounds protected state multiplicities before cancellations in an index, and gives an algebraic account of the finite-rank reorganization of protected trace operators.

papers.title: Linear Approximations Provide Rigorous Conditions for Phase Locking in Oscillator Networks and Power Grids
papers.abstract: Synchronization is a fundamental collective phenomenon in many natural and engineered networks. The stable operation of oscillator networks, such as electric power grids, requires phase locking with phase differences across edges below a given threshold. A central question is whether a given network supports such a state. In this contribution, we extend a convex optimization formulation of the nonlinear fixed point equations of the Kuramoto model, that also describe lossless power grids. Based on this formulation, we derive rigorous and tight bounds on the error introduced by an arbitrary approximation of the original model, in particular linear approximations. The bounds yield edge-wise regions of trust around the approximation, within which the true nonlinear solution must lie. They further provide sufficient and necessary conditions for phase locking under prescribed phase difference limits. Numerical experiments show that the bounds are tight over a broad range of parameters.

papers.title: Attitude Estimation of Falcon 9 Rocket Body Based on Photometric Characteristics
papers.abstract: The proliferation of space debris, driven by increasingly frequent space activities, poses a severe risk to operational satellites and future missions. Consequently, the surveillance and characterization of space objects have become critical. Current methods for attitude estimation of space objects often rely on target-specific models, such as those with a closed set of facets, and typically employ nonlinear filtering or machine learning techniques. However, these approaches often lack general applicability. This study proposes a more general approach to attitude estimation based on photometric light curves. We define a loss function that quantifies the discrepancy between the measured light curve and a theoretical model parameterized by the attitude parameters. By leveraging automatic differentiation to compute the gradients of this function, we use a gradient descent algorithm to achieve rapid and accurate attitude estimation. The proposed method provides a versatile and efficient framework for attitude estimation, overcoming the target-specificity limitations of existing techniques, with the parameters estimation time reduced to 15 seconds and the mean square error lowered to three decimal places. Validation on the third-party database demonstrates that the method exhibits strong generalization capability.

papers.title: CADS: Measuring the Incremental Contribution of LLM Proposers in Sequential Biological Screens
papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to guide sequential biological screens, yet standard evaluations rely on raw hit counts that conflate a proposer's value with the discovery capacity of the underlying algorithmic harness. Adaptive sampling and corrupted experimental readouts also leave standard feedback comparisons without a false-discovery guarantee. We present Certified Agentic Discovery Screens (CADS), an error-controlled measurement framework that quantifies a proposer's incremental value against an identical LLM-free loop. By integrating capped likelihood-ratio bounds, e-processes, and complete-family e-BH, CADS controls the terminal false discovery rate under the stated null and corruption conditions despite arbitrary dependence, adaptive sampling, and optional stopping. In DepMap-backed simulations, CADS exposes two evaluation artifacts: the LLM-free harness alone clears the feedback gate, and raw origin counts overstate LLM contributions because LLM picks displace fallback discoveries. On the initial 20 seeds, supplying tested-candidate history to Qwen2.5-7B shifts its net contribution from +0.35, with a 95% interval covering zero, to +2.90, with the interval above zero. This initial net effect did not persist in a 50-seed matched-quota replication. These results support net gain over an LLM-free loop, measured between separately certified sets, as the appropriate measure of proposer contribution.

papers.title: AdamPM: Memory-Efficient LLM Optimization via Moment Pooling
papers.abstract: Adam is widely used for training large language models (LLMs) owing to its strong optimization performance and training stability, but its element-wise estimation for the first and second moments incur substantial memory overhead. Although numerous memory-efficient optimizers have been proposed, many incur additional computational overhead or require additional tuning of hyperparameters. Consequently, Adam remains a dominant and reliable choice for LLM pre-training. We propose AdamPM (Adam with Pooled Moments), a simple and memory-efficient variant of Adam that groups adjacent moment entries along the row or column dimension and represents each group by a single shared mean. AdamPM can well inherit Adam's hyperparameter settings and is readily integrated into existing Adam optimizer implementations, with less memory overhead. We systematically investigate pooling of both first and second moment estimates and identify second moment pooling as the effective design. With a group size of $s$, AdamPM reduces second moment memory to $1/s$ of the original requirement. Extensive experiments on language model pretraining, fine-tuning and multimodal learning demonstrate that AdamPM maintains model performance and training speed while substantially reducing optimizer-state memory. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/jixiaowei95/AdamPM}.

papers.title: Severity-Channel Conditioning: An Injection-Level Study for Consumer-Device Deblurring
papers.abstract: Motion-deblurring models lose substantial accuracy when transferred from professional cameras to smartphone-derived imagery. This paper studies whether a severity descriptor, partly derived from the paired sharp target, helps adaptation on the iPhoneBlur consumer-device benchmark. Under a shared update budget, input concatenation of a severity map is compared with global feature modulation by capture metadata, spatial feature modulation by the severity map, and a tier-contrastive output objective, together with an unconditioned spectral-loss control, all fine-tuned from the same domain-adapted latent-diffusion baseline. The primary experiment is an oracle diagnostic: target-derived information is supplied at inference. For the evaluated model pair, input concatenation improves overall peak signal-to-noise ratio from 31.23 to 31.30 dB, whereas feature modulation, the contrastive objective, and the spectral-loss control do not exceed the baseline. The gain is positive on 87.2% of test images and on 14 of 15 held-out source videos; this video-level analysis describes the evaluated checkpoint pair and does not establish robustness to retraining, and three training seeds are reported separately. The input-level gain recurs on a transformer backbone. In one exploratory run, zeroing the channel at inference retains most of the gain in peak signal-to-noise ratio but lowers structural similarity below the baseline. A normalized-step diagnostic does not support the expected larger-gradient explanation. The results characterize the evaluated configurations and do not establish injection location as the sole cause, a spatial-locality mechanism, or a reliable deployment advantage.

papers.title: Extraction of All Partial-Wave Interaction Parameters via Femtoscopy: The Central-Force Case
papers.abstract: We present a universal femtoscopic method to extract the source size and central-force interaction parameters for arbitrary partial waves from experimental data, with the interaction parameters defined in the effective-range expansion. The method is based on the Wronskian determinant and is applicable to both the Coulomb and non-Coulomb cases. This approach is numerically verified against simulated neutron-neutron and proton-proton correlation data obtained from the Reid potential.

papers.title: TCMScience: An Autonomous Scientist for Traditional Chinese Medicine
papers.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) research connects classical texts, medicinal entities, molecular assays, computational predictions, and clinical studies. An autonomous research agent must preserve the inferential boundaries between these evidence types while coordinating analysis across heterogeneous resources. We introduce TCMScience, a scientific knowledge-discovery agent that separates language-model proposals from execution and release authority. Its architecture combines a trusted kernel, a scientific compiler, and claim-support contracts: plans are compiled into typed operations, execution is bounded by explicit permissions, and candidate findings are checked against source provenance, study design, and claim scope before release. The full capability registry contains 117 public-source connectors with 444 typed operations across 29 domains and 150 native tools across 12 domains; the TCM data hub catalogs 136 databases, 76 dataset specifications, and 84,294 formula-source records. These resources support model-independent workflows through browser and local execution interfaces. In a network-pharmacology analysis of Gegen Qinlian Tang, replacing the whole-proteome background with the assayed-protein background changed the number of significant pathways from 66 to zero; incorporating inactive screening records identified nine pathways, including drug-metabolism signals retained as mechanistic hypotheses. A governance ablation over 121 constructed erroneous outputs spanning 26 classes released 121 errors without governance, 57 with the domain layer, seven with the kernel, and zero with both layers. All 10 compliant controls were retained. These results establish complementary control of known failure modes and show how explicit evidence contracts change the conclusions an agent is permitted to report.

papers.title: Dynamic self-ensemble on multi-exit residual vision transformer for small-data image classification
papers.abstract: Vision Transformer (ViT) has garnered increased attention for image classification in recent years. However, ViT is notorious for its data-hungry problem as it achieves high-performance results when only trained on large-size datasets. In this paper, we study how ViT specifically works on small-scale datasets with limited data where the availability of image data is often constrained in practice, especially in fields such as medical imaging. To mitigate the issue, we designed a multi-stage residual ViT, dubbed ReSEViT, with the self-ensemble method to utilize multi-level information from intermediate features. Due to the complex decision boundaries for classifications, relying on a single classifier can lead to prediction errors. Hence, we propose a new learning method for ViT, named self-ensemble learning, which ensembles multi-stage classifiers in a single model. Our self-ensemble comprises a novel approach, Dynamic Learner Selection (DLS), to adaptively select the importance of different stages. ReSEViT incorporates residual token embeddings which is a ResNet-like block to model effective local structures alongside with transformer blocks in each stage. The integration of residual tokens and self-ensemble learning into a multi-stage ViT highlights the reduction in redundancy, prediction error and variance while maintaining an efficient model size for small-scale image datasets.

papers.title: Refuse the Harm, Complete the Task via Graph-of-Rules Planning for LLM-Enabled Robots
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in embodied AI for robotic manipulation and planning, but their deployment in physical systems exposes vulnerabilities such as jailbreak attacks that induce unsafe behavior. Existing inference-time defenses are mainly evaluated on short instructions containing a single hazard, whereas realistic tasks may interleave safe and unsafe sub-tasks, conceal hazardous steps, or combine individually safe actions into unsafe outcomes. Such compound instructions make it harder for a single safety decision to distinguish hazardous sub-tasks from legitimate ones, risking either overlooking the hazard or rejecting the whole instruction. We introduce safe task completion, a task that requires an LLM-enabled robot to refuse the harmful part of an instruction while completing its legitimate part. To address this problem, we propose RuleGraph, a multi-agent Graph-of-Rules planning framework that distributes safety enforcement across multiple reasoning and verification stages. Five cooperating agents are used to ground general safety principles into world-specific rules, assess the instruction's sub-tasks in context, and derive a safe goal from the legitimate ones. Planning toward this goal is then organized as a graph of rule-specific nodes, where higher-level nodes inherit the union of their parents' rules, and candidate plans are progressively verified and aggregated until a single plan satisfies every relevant rule. In this way, RuleGraph reduces reliance on a single centralized safety decision. We evaluate RuleGraph on pure-attack and compound instructions across two benchmarks in two environments using Attack Success Rate (ASR) and Task Success Rate (TSR). RuleGraph reduces ASR to 0% on both benchmarks while achieving the highest TSR among all methods, reaching 98.57% on the RoboGuard benchmark and 84.54% on our long-horizon compound instructions.

papers.title: SCOPE-VSR: A Broad-Coverage Training Dataset for Video Super-Resolution
papers.abstract: Open-domain video super-resolution (VSR) requires temporally coherent details across widely varying scenes and subjects. However, existing training datasets are often semantically imbalanced and insufficiently diverse. We address this data bottleneck with a structured curation pipeline for open-domain VSR, SCOPE. In this pipeline, we combine task-oriented video selection with hierarchical semantic rebalancing. Applying this pipeline to a large-scale collection of data sources, we construct the SCOPE-VSR dataset for training and SCOPE-test for testing. SCOPE-VSR has approximately 27k videos and provides balanced and diverse coverage of various real-world scenarios and subjects. We further develop GraCo-VSR, a novel framework for one-step video restoration. GraCo-VSR adopts a reliability-aware design with explicit supervision to reduce degradation-induced distortions in motion and texture guidance, allowing the model to benefit more effectively from the diverse training content in SCOPE-VSR. Evaluations show that our model achieves strong reconstruction fidelity and perceptual quality. Our code is available at: https://github.com/gyliao2768/SCOPE-VSR.

papers.title: RoMo-GS: Efficient Online 3D Gaussian Splatting for Robot Mapping via Exposure-Integrated Motion Blur
papers.abstract: Online 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is emerging as a practical way to build a representation for robotics applications. However, deploying it on real-world platforms exposes multiple challenges. Rapid maneuvers of a robot induce motion-blurred images, which corrupt the reconstructed geometry and cause camera pose drift. Furthermore, the number of Gaussians grows without bound during continuous online mapping. In this study, we present RoMo-GS, an online 3DGS system designed to address these challenges. Instead of averaging N discrete sub-frames as in prior motion blur-aware 3DGS, we analytically integrate each projected Gaussian over the exposure interval, yielding an O(1) complexity per Gaussian. Building on this, we bound the Gaussians' growth with a Hessian-based pruning score, while jointly refining pose, velocity, and Gaussians with Adam and an online LM step over the Gaussians. On multiple public datasets and a self-collected dataset, RoMo-GS matches or exceeds offline deblurring 3DGS methods in rendering quality while running 15--150x faster, and operates online at competitive quality with about 20% fewer Gaussians than the online 3DGS baseline.

papers.title: Length-convexity and domination for Hitchin representations
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g\geq 2$. For any $n\geq 3$, let $\text{Hit}_n(S)$ be the Hitchin component and let $\text{Hit}_n(S)^\prime$ be the subset of representations that take values in $\mathrm{PSp}_{2m}(\mathbb{R})$ if $n=2m$ and $\mathrm{PSO}(m,m+1)$ if $n=2m+1$. In this note we prove that for any Hitchin representation $ρ\in \text{Hit}_n(S)$ there is $j \in \text{Hit}_n(S)^\prime$ such that $ρ$ dominates $j$ in the Hilbert length spectrum; this confirms a conjecture of Lee-Zhang and, independently, Tholozan who had proved this for $n=3$. The key step is establishing a convexity of the Hilbert length function in the Bonahon-Dreyer parametrization of $\text{Hit}_n(S)$; this uses a result from the recent work of Barman-Gupta. We also prove these convexity and domination results for translation length functions and their spectra.

papers.title: IntriAdapt: Generalizable Intrinsic-Guided Test-Time Adaptation for Metric Geometry Estimation
papers.abstract: Recovering metric 3D geometry from images is fundamentally ill-posed due to perspective projection ambiguity. Current geometry models incorporate supplied or predicted intrinsics during inference, but do not use them to supervise model adaptation. To refine these predictions, test-time adaptation (TTA) typically relies on external depth measurements. In this paper, we instead use camera intrinsics as an output-side geometric verifier. Comparing the point cloud's viewing rays with those defined by the known intrinsics yields a direct measure of geometric inconsistency. We propose \textit{IntriAdapt}, a TTA framework that minimizes this closed-form geometric residual. By optimizing a lightweight LoRA adapter on a frozen geometry foundation model, our method aligns the prediction with the specific camera model without depth sensors or external priors. We further extend this approach to video sequences, demonstrating that adapting a short sequence generalizes to other sequences captured by the same camera. The adapted model processes held-out images in a feed-forward pass, without repeating optimization for each frame. Experiments on ten single-image and seven sequence benchmarks across multiple base models show that \textit{IntriAdapt} consistently outperforms both unadapted and oracle-intrinsics baselines in metric accuracy and relative geometry.

papers.title: Fabric retrofit scenario analysis under uncertainty for an urban housing stock using machine learning
papers.abstract: Fabric retrofit is central to decarbonising housing, and planning it depends on expected savings and their uncertainty. This study asks which upgrade saves most per dwelling and across a housing portfolio, how uncertain the savings are, and whether upgrade order matters. We propose an uncertainty-aware framework that converts predicted changes in energy performance certificate scores after wall, roof and window upgrades into standardised energy-cost savings and emission reductions. Six machine-learning models predict the 1-100 Standard Assessment Procedure (SAP) energy-cost and environmental impact (EI) emission scores from 17 certificate descriptors. Each model's errors on similar dwellings give calibrated prediction intervals. A global-best strategy applies the most accurate model throughout; a sample-specific strategy chooses each dwelling's model using these local errors. The analysis covers 103,414 officially registered dwellings in Westminster, London. CatBoost was the global-best model, with mean absolute errors of 3.487 SAP and 4.379 EI points on held-out dwellings. Both strategies projected similar savings; under global-best, roof insulation saved most per dwelling, GBP 203 annually (uncertainty range 176-229), and wall insulation most across the portfolio, GBP 6.09 million annually (uncertainty range 5.69-6.72). For 5,382 dwellings needing all three upgrades, every order delivered the same final package, yet installing roofs, walls, then windows a year apart accumulated 54% more projected cost savings over three years than the reverse order. Emission reductions followed the same pattern. Using only certificate data, the framework helps local authorities rank measures for dwellings and portfolios and sequence upgrades to bring savings forward.

papers.title: Rethinking Social Simulation in Open-Population Systems: From Persistent Agents to Communication Processes
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have enabled social simulation with persistent agents, where fixed computational individuals maintain internal states and interact over time. However, large-scale social networks are inherently open-population systems: the participating population changes over time, users enter and leave dynamically, and only a sparse subset becomes observable through communication at any given time. In such systems, persistent account identities do not provide continuously observable individual-state trajectories, making recursively maintained psychological states insufficiently grounded in empirical observations. We therefore shift the simulation target from persistent individual trajectories to the observable evolution of social communication, modeling who participates, what they communicate, and how these communications shape subsequent system dynamics. We instantiate this formulation with participant activation from a global user pool, collective state transition, and an LLM policy for communication generation, while explicitly separating environmental inputs from endogenous system evolution. Across five Qwen backbones, our framework reduces average KL divergence by 71.2% over Direct LLM and 35.0% over MF-LLM, with boundary and counterfactual experiments further validating the proposed modeling boundaries. Our results support communication-centered simulation as a principled formulation for long-horizon open-population social systems. Project Website: https://ai4ss.github.io/OpenSim/

papers.title: From Candidate Admission to Task-Level Return: Auditing LLM-Generated Code under Execution Contracts
papers.abstract: Admission rules retain generated programs, whereas selection policies return one candidate per task. We audit how these decisions interact with execution contracts in two separately frozen, disjoint HumanEvalPlus cohorts, each comprising 32 tasks, four samples per task per profile and two served profiles. Under the inline execution contract, a structural-and-self-test screen admits 4-9 expanded-suite nonpasses per 80-107 admissions and excludes 14-43 suite passes per 128 planned attempts. A restricted module-supply condition adds 20 and 14 passing admissions for one profile in the respective cohorts, plus one follow-up nonpass, and reduces the excluded suite passes to 14-23. All fixed first-admitted outcomes and abstentions remain unchanged. In the original pool, the added passes enter already all-passing admitted pools; in the follow-up, four of 24 common sample orders lose one passed task. Selected-subset diagnostics separately address registration-sensitive completion and reference-relative assertion disagreement, accounting for input domains and comparator tolerances. In these high-pass pools, candidate retention and task-level return diverge and are reported separately. Results are conditional on the saved pools, contracts and pinned suites; downstream training effects are unmeasured.

papers.title: Solving a Giant Rubik's Cube with a Quadruped Robot
papers.abstract: Pedipulating a freestanding articulated object requires controlling its pose and internal configuration while maintaining balance. We demonstrate this capability by autonomously solving a giant Rubik's Cube with a quadruped using only its feet. The task demands repeated precise interactions, since unintended layer motion can invalidate subsequent operations. We develop an onboard RGB-D perception pipeline that estimates the cube's metric pose and its full color state from partial views acquired through locomotion and flipping. A planner converts the computed solve into robot-executable skill sequences. Learned whole-body skills reorient the cube while preserving its layer configuration and turn its layers with one foot pinning the cube as the other pushes. We train these skills using reinforcement learning with privileged observations and distill them into policies that map onboard depth and proprioception to joint targets. The deployed policies tolerate variations in relative robot-cube placement and recover from external disturbances. The system completes three autonomous hardware solves, each about 30 steps over 8-9 minutes. These results show that combining onboard perception with coordinated pedipulation enables a quadruped to complete extended multi-step physical tasks. Additional material can be found at: https://leggedrobotics.github.io/rubik-skills/

papers.title: HSPR: Recovering Software-Agent Benchmark Scores via Hierarchical Posterior Inference
papers.abstract: Evaluating software agents on a full benchmark is expensive. A small task subset can preserve agent rankings while yielding inaccurate scores. Historical responses provide useful structure, but tasks with identical source responses can have different outcomes for a new target agent. We introduce Hierarchical Score Posterior Recovery (HSPR), which combines source-fitted response factors with uncertain group success rates. Observed target outcomes update the posteriors over the target latent state and group rates; posterior-guided acquisition selects subsequent tasks. Its score-based criterion equals the expected one-step reduction in full-score posterior variance. Observed successes and posterior-predictive counts for unqueried tasks yield a full-score posterior. The final estimate uses its median with source-selected calibration. At a 10% task budget on four task banks from the SWE-bench family, HSPR achieves the lowest mean absolute error (MAE) on three banks and the lowest maximum absolute error (MaxErr) on all four among the methods compared. Removing group uncertainty or replacing adaptive queries increases macro MAE in the respective controls. Macro MAE decreases across 5-20% budgets. Code and project resources are publicly available.

papers.title: Human Exposition of Claude's 2/3 Theorem on the zeros of zeta
papers.abstract: We expose Claude's proof that $N_0(T)\ge 0.6725 N(T)$ where $N(T)$ is the number of zeros of zeta satisfying $0<\mathop{\mathrm{Re}}ρ\le T$, and $N_0(T)$ the number of those zeros that are simple and on the critical line. Unconditionally it was only known that $N_0(T)\ge 0.4166 N(T)$. This proof is simpler than the previous ones and takes a different approach.

papers.title: How Much Do Activation Monitors Benefit from Original Model Computations?
papers.abstract: One powerful way to safeguard AI systems is to monitor their internal computations--where signs of undesirable behavior might be more easily detectable than from models' inputs and outputs alone. However, recent studies begin to question the premise that activations provide a unique window into model behavior. In this paper, we study how much of activation monitors' success depends on access to the original behavior-generating computations. Within a fixed choice of target model and monitoring architecture, we compare how well monitors trained and evaluated on trajectories that differ in computational context can predict the behavior of the original execution, after the transcript is changed in a controlled manner (e.g., its exact text, or chat formatting). We first find that much performance can be recovered without access to the original behavior-generating trace (in up to 4 models across 2 counterfactual monitoring tasks), but a mild yet consistent advantage to native-trained monitors remains, outperforming strongest controls by up to 0.014 AUROC. Interestingly, we find monitors trained with native access have notable uplift on original examples whose behavioral label changes under paraphrasing. We further find this a useful lens to expose limitations of baselines that use simple forms of privileged information (i.e., answer logit margins). While our results show the advantage of native monitor access is modest in aggregate, they highlight the importance of evaluations that identify if and when original model computations provide additional predictive value.

papers.title: Safety Kernel: Mechanistic Alignment for Cross-Lingual Defense in LLMs
papers.abstract: The safety capabilities of large language models (LLMs) are highly uneven across different languages, often allowing cross-lingual attacks to bypass safety guardrails. Existing alignment methods predominantly rely on external alignment signals and provide limited insight into underlying neuron-level mechanisms, making it difficult to provide a unified internal target for cross-lingual safety interventions. To address this, we analyze cross-lingual safety behavior at the neuron level and identify a compact set of safety-related neurons shared across languages, termed the safety kernel (SK). Specifically, we first utilize multilingual parallel safe and unsafe prompts to compute safety contrast with activation responsiveness (SCAR) scores, identifying language-wise safety-neuron candidates from internal activation patterns. We then intersect the resulting language-wise safety-neuron sets to obtain the SK, and validate its functional relevance to cross-lingual safety behavior through activation suppression and activation-state transfer interventions. Finally, building on the SK coordinates, we introduce SK-Masked LoRA, which constrains LoRA adaptation to the feed-forward network (FFN) output dimensions corresponding to the SK, thereby focusing safety-related changes on the cross-lingually shared neuron coordinates. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SK-Masked LoRA substantially reduces attack success rates across multiple languages, including languages excluded from SK discovery, while intervening on only a small fraction of internal neuron coordinates and producing generally limited changes in the model's general capabilities.

papers.title: Locally convex spaces with hemicompact weak* dual
papers.abstract: For a locally convex space $L$ let $L'_σ$ denote its dual endowed with the weak* topology $σ(L',L)$. We prove that $L'_σ$ is hemicompact if and only if $L$ with the Mackey topology $τ(L,L')$ is metrizable and barrelled, and if and only if $L'_σ$ is $σ$-compact and quasi-complete. The key step is that a hemicompact $L'_σ$ is quasi-complete. The Mackey topology $τ(L,L')$ is metrizable if and only if $L'$ is a countable union of absolutely convex weak*-compact sets; spaces with normable barrelled Mackey topology are characterized similarly. As a consequence, a metrizable (in particular, normed) space $L$ is barrelled if and only if $L'_σ$ is hemicompact. For function spaces we obtain: $(C_k(X))'_σ$ is hemicompact if and only if $X$ is hemicompact, and $(C_p(X))'_σ$ is hemicompact if and only if $X$ is countable and all compact subsets of $X$ are finite.

papers.title: SIESTA-QCOMP: Bridging Classical and Quantum Computing for Strongly Correlated Systems
papers.abstract: Density Functional Theory (DFT) is the established workhorse of computational materials science, yet it faces fundamental challenges with strongly correlated electrons, such as in transition metal complexes and bond-breaking processes. While quantum computing offers a theoretically exact path to resolve these problems, current hardware limitations prohibit fully quantum simulations of realistic material systems. To bridge this gap, we present SIESTA-QCOMP, a modular suite embedding quantum methodologies within DFT. Harnessing SIESTA's localised basis set, we implement a projection-based embedding scheme that treats the bulk environment classically while mapping the strongly correlated "impurity" subspace to a quantum processor. The architecture uses a socket-based driver to orchestrate workflows between the Fortran-based SIESTA engine and Python-based frameworks like Qiskit, ensuring high interoperability. We detail the hybrid workflow, currently utilising a Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), and discuss the road map toward methods such as Sample-based Quantum Diagonalisation (SQD). We illustrate the framework on an hypothetical iron porphyrin calculation and argue that such hybrid architectures are not merely interim solutions but essential foundations for integrating quantum utility into materials design, as envisioned by our broader QCOMP4DFT initiative.

papers.title: Task Offloading and Resource Allocation for Deterministic Service Provisioning in the IoT-Edge-Cloud Continuum
papers.abstract: Future networks will seamlessly integrate computing and communication resources within a unified ecosystem of IoT devices, edge nodes, and cloud servers, forming an IoT-edge-cloud continuum. Within such an ecosystem, tasks can be dynamically offloaded to leverage resources across the continuum and efficiently scale with demand. Task offloading has traditionally focused on minimizing task execution latency or energy consumption. In contrast, we propose a deterministic task offloading and resource allocation scheme for the joint management of communication and computing resources to support services with deterministic service-level requirements. The proposed scheme aims to maximize the number of tasks completed on time, rather than minimizing the latency of individual tasks. To do so, it exploits variable task latency requirements to distribute the workload across the continuum. It can also prioritize high-priority tasks under resource scarcity. Numerical evaluations demonstrate that a deterministic task offloading strategy scales more effectively and can better guarantee timely task completion by balancing resource utilization across the continuum.

papers.title: Galactic warps constrain equivalence-principle violation in the dark sector
papers.abstract: Current measurements of the expansion of the Universe allow for the presence of evolving dark energy, distinct from a cosmological constant, with an equation of state that seems to violate the null energy condition. One notable explanation for this behaviour is that the dark energy interacts with the dark matter, violating the equivalence principle yet evading conventional laboratory and astrophysical constraints. Such models produce fifth forces acting only on dark matter. We show how such forces separate halo and stellar disk centres, creating a potential gradient across the disk that warps it into a cup shape. Measuring the warps of $4\times10^3$ edge-on disks in Sloan Digital Sky Survey images and modelling the fifth-force signal together with competing baryonic effects, we find no sign of the predicted correlation between the measured warps and the fifth-force field. This constrains the fifth-force strength relative to gravity to $ΔG/G_N<7.7\times10^{-4}$ at 95% credibility (or $<1.7\times10^{-3}$ once systematic uncertainties are included) for force ranges of 8 Mpc and above. In the infinite-range limit of a scalar rolling today, even the conservative bound is three times stronger than the tightest cosmological bound (which, unlike ours, depends on the scalar's cosmological evolution) and about two orders of magnitude below other astrophysical bounds. It disfavours at 2-3$σ$ the couplings preferred by recent fits of interacting dark energy to cosmological data unless gravitational screening is invoked.

papers.title: Beyond Geometric Closure: Measuring and Diagnosing Mechanical Consistency in Visual Dynamics
papers.abstract: Visual accuracy, geometric validity, and agreement with applied forces are distinct requirements for visual dynamics. We introduce a diagnostic framework that connects reaction-free SI measurements to controlled interventions on coordinate readout, training integration, and actuator response. Reference replay calibrates the measurement path, while continuous scoring exposes progress against fixed engineering targets. With three seeds per setting, we evaluate KeyCLD and CON across 343 planar assemblies at 64/256 pixels and V-JEPA + AC and LingBot-VA on 100 shared spatial test assemblies. CON reduces image MSE by 37.6%/37.2% relative to persistence, yet neither planar model attains valid native geometry. At 256 pixels, calibrated RGB replay places forecast errors far above the reference measurement floor. Exact-state KeyCLD has identical geometric pass rates under Euler and RK4 training, yet its score rises from 52.65 to 64.30 as force and energy errors decrease. In both spatial pathways, CAD/IK reconstruction restores geometry while mean actuator residuals exceed five times the engineering targets. These diagnoses distinguish coordinate correction, numerical improvement, and persistent force-response errors, guiding targeted improvements to visual dynamics.

papers.title: Lyapunov-Krasovsky Functionals and the Existence of Unbounded Solutions of Functional-Differential Equations of Retarded Type
papers.abstract: In this paper, the concepts of unboundedness and partial unboundedness of solutions of functional-differential equations of retarded type are introduced. On the basis of the method of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals, sufficient conditions for the existence of partially unbounded solutions are obtained. As corollaries, sufficient conditions for the existence of unbounded solutions are obtained.

papers.title: A mechanism for TCP-aware Active Queue Management in packet-forwarding devices
papers.abstract: The deployment of Active Queue Management (AQM) policies is known to be a promising solution to bufferbloat, the problem of persistently-full large buffers in Internet routers. However, most AQMs involve tunable parameters, and some require awareness of the characteristics of the transport-layer protocol implemented at the end systems, thereby rendering their deployment infeasible. We consider one such AQM-- a threshold-based queue policy which requires the packet-dropping threshold to be co-designed with relevant TCP parameters. We propose a mechanism that detects network congestion, estimates the congestion window evolution in the end hosts, estimates the required TCP parameter, and produces an optimal value of the packet-dropping threshold. Arguments based on analysis of the TCP fluid model are presented to substantiate the proposed mechanism. A simulation-based performance evaluation reveals the effectiveness of the proposed mechanism, compared to some widely implemented queue policies, in terms of various user- and system-oriented metrics. The proposed mechanism is particularly well-suited for implementation in Software Defined Networks (SDN) where the algorithms can run in the SDN controller and the packet-dropping threshold can be implemented in the data-plane switches through open interfaces.

papers.title: Fluxion: A Differentiable DSP Runtime from Training GPU to Real-Time Edge
papers.abstract: Native real-time audio engines meet audio deadlines but are hard to connect to machine-learning workflows, while tensor frameworks integrate with machine learning but process audio as offline batches without timing guarantees; runtime layers built on them inherit the host's scheduling and deployment footprint. This paper presents Fluxion, a Rust audio DSP runtime for cascaded second-order sections, FIR filters, and delay-line effects. Fluxion implements the parts that are specific to DSP: closed-form filter design, forward kernels, analytic adjoints for the recursion, and stability checks. It relies on existing libraries for the autodiff graph, GPU code generation (tested here on CUDA), and array interchange. One graph algebra is lowered to a differentiable training engine and to an allocation-free real-time engine; between them, a trained graph is checked for stability and frozen into a versioned artifact that an edge device checks again before playback. We compare Fluxion with six framework-hosted and native baselines under one float32 protocol. Among the systems that compute the exact recursion, Fluxion has the highest GPU throughput when data stays on the device and the highest throughput on most CPU workloads, while its CPU training step is slower than those of torchaudio and GRAFX. Its test suite checks the audio thread for allocations with an instrumented allocator, and we report measured latency tails. Fluxion is open source at \url{https://github.com/matteospanio/fluxion}.

papers.title: Narratives Mislead: An Empirical Study of How LLMs Misjudge CVSS Severity in Bug Bounty Reports
papers.abstract: Bug bounty platforms receive vulnerability reports faster than vendors can triage them, and Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly considered for assigning the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) severity that drives prioritization. Prior evaluations score short CVE descriptions and report accuracy, but deployment depends on how models err, not only how often. CVSS gives each metric a formal meaning that departs from how researchers describe impact in narrative reports, and model rationales suggest that errors concentrate where the two diverge; we ask whether this pattern is systematic. From 4,281 publicly disclosed reports mined from Huntr and HackerOne, we build a benchmark of 240 Huntr reports with vendor-validated CVSS vectors and evaluate eight LLMs under four prompting strategies and fine-tuning, measuring errors by severity class and score and analysing sub-vectors on individual reports. The best prompting configuration reaches only 49.58% level accuracy, ten points above always predicting the majority level, and fine-tuning a 7B model raises this to at most 56.25%, an optimistic upper bound. Errors are directional: models overestimate far more often than they underestimate, and they almost never recognize low-severity vulnerabilities. We trace these errors to three semantic boundaries that the specification draws and narrative reports blur: potential versus realized impact, impact magnitude versus authorization scope, and uncertainty versus the worst case. Because the violations originate partly in the report, we close with an exploratory case study: on four reports, a boundary-aligned, exploit-free report structure lowered a frontier model's score where the narrative invited an unclaimed account takeover, but left the metrics a report does not settle open, and the two published labels disagreed on three of the four reports.

papers.title: Uncovering Semantic Hierarchies in Text-Attributed Graphs via Variational EM-based LLM-GNN Synergy
papers.abstract: While hierarchical structures are intrinsic to organizing human knowledge, current representation learning on text-attributed graphs predominantly operates on flat semantic spaces, overlooking the rich coarse-to-fine granularity inherent in real-world data. To bridge this gap, we propose SHiFT, which synergizes the reasoning power of LLMs with the structural representation capability of GNNs within an Expectation-Maximization (EM) paradigm. In the E-step, we harness LLMs as expert taxonomists to induce an explicit semantic tree, introducing a lightweight Mapping & Diagnosis strategy that reduces inference costs by surgically updating the hierarchy only when anomalies are detected. In the M-step, we align the GNN encoder with this induced hierarchy from complementary perspectives, including clustering partition, topological skeleton, and semantic concepts. Theoretical analysis interprets SHiFT as a generalized Variational EM algorithm. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SHiFT not only achieves state-of-the-art performance but also uncovers high-quality, human-readable taxonomies. Our code can be found at https://github.com/Cloudy1225/SHiFT.

papers.title: Static tidal Love numbers of Schwarzschild and non-Schwarzschild black holes in quadratic gravity
papers.abstract: We calculate the static electric quadrupolar response of black holes in four-dimensional quadratic gravity, with action $R-αC^2+βR^2$. The Schwarzschild solution has zero massless gravitational Love number under the stated boundary conditions. A numerical non-Schwarzschild solution instead has a nonzero negative response. At $α/r_h^2=1/2$, we find $λ_E/r_h^5\simeq-0.1224928$ and $k_2^{(r_h)}\simeq-0.1837391$, with a final outer-endpoint change in $k_2^{(r_h)}$ of about $1.60\times10^{-7}$. We explain how the background is obtained by shooting and how the tidal solution is selected by matching at an intermediate radius. The perturbations are written in Kodama--Ishibashi gauge-invariant variables. After the scalar-curvature perturbation is excluded by horizon regularity and the absence of an applied scalar tide, the remaining static sector has three coupled second-order radial equations. We define the curvature amplitudes in these equations and describe why simple attempts to separate them fail. The coupling scan shows a negative response approaching zero near the Schwarzschild intersection. We also explain why this full-theory result does not conflict with the removal of curvature-squared operators in a perturbative low-energy expansion.

papers.title: Infinitesimally Euclidean metric surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove the equivalence of several notions of infinitesimally Euclidean-like behaviour for metric surfaces appearing in the literature. We obtain in particular that metric surfaces with property (ET) are universally infinitesimally Hilbertian.

papers.title: UDL-RT: A unified differentiable all-sky microwave radiative transfer model with learnable parameterizations
papers.abstract: Radiance-based retrievals and data assimilation require radiative transfer models (RTMs) to simulate radiances and quantify their sensitivities to atmospheric and surface conditions. Conventional RTMs often rely on separately maintained forward, tangent-linear, and adjoint codes, complicating model development and extension. Here, we present the Unified Differentiable and Learnable Radiative Transfer model (UDL-RT), a PyTorch-based framework for all-sky microwave radiative transfer that couples neural-network (NN) parameterizations of gaseous absorption, hydrometeor bulk scattering properties (BSPs), and ocean surface emissivity with an explicit radiative transfer solver in a unified differentiable computational graph. Automatic differentiation directly computes Jacobians with respect to input variables, reducing the model maintenance burden. The NN parameterizations offer flexible representations of complex nonlinear relationships. For example, the NN gas-absorption parameterization reduces the standard deviation of brightness-temperature (TB) errors by approximately 60-85% in the water-vapour channels compared with linear regression. Moreover, UDL-RT propagates loss gradients to trainable parameters to optimize physical parameterizations against observations, with GPU-accelerated batched computation supporting efficient iterative learning. Using Microwave Humidity Sounder-2 (MWHS-2) observations, we optimize the snow BSP parameterization through gradient-based learning. The optimized parameterization improves agreement between simulated and observed TB distributions and reduces the systematic bias and skewness of observation-minus-background (O-B) departures. Overall, UDL-RT integrates radiance simulation, sensitivity analysis, and parameterization optimization within a unified framework, supporting future remote sensing retrieval and data assimilation applications.

papers.title: Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model
papers.abstract: We introduce Muse Glimmer, an open-source 30B parameter causal language model with perception encoder, purpose-built for autonomous agentic tasks on consumer hardware. Muse Glimmer integrates multi-step reasoning, reliable tool use and failure recovery into a single model that runs locally on consumer devices without requiring cloud infrastructure. The model accepts text and image inputs and produces text outputs, was trained on data from over a hundred languages, and is quantized to approximately 4-bit precision for efficient single-GPU inference. Muse Glimmer achieves state-of-the-art performance for its size class on agentic benchmarks, setting a new standard compared to the models of its size: Gemma4-31B and Qwen3.6-27B on tool use, multi-step planning, and agentic task completion. We release the model under the Apache 2.0 license to foster open-source development of capable, safe, local AI agents.

papers.title: Signed FK percolation in Ising spin glasses
papers.abstract: We introduce signed Fortuin-Kasteleyn (FK) percolation for the +/-J random-interaction Ising model to characterize nonzero uniform magnetization density and two-replica overlap within the class of Gibbs distributions whose infinite-volume Edwards-Sokal (ES)/FK representation has at most one infinite FK cluster almost surely. The construction refines ordinary FK connectivity by retaining the parity of coupling products along open paths. Using the infinite-volume ES representation and its DLR equations, we study pairs of companion objects and the compatible spin assignments on them. In one replica, companions are defined by positive-parity FK connections. For extremal states satisfying the infinite-cluster assumption and almost-sure existence of companion densities along the chosen van Hove sequence, nonzero limiting expected magnetization density is equivalent to density distinguishability of the companions of the infinite FK cluster. For two independent replicas, companions are defined by FK connections coherent in parity. For products of extremal one-replica states satisfying the infinite-cluster assumption and almost-sure existence of the companion densities along the chosen sequence, density distinguishability of the companions is equivalent to nonzero limiting expected mutual overlap. For two independent replicas drawn from the same extremal state, this specializes to the Edwards-Anderson self-overlap.

papers.title: Selm: Self-Evolving Library Management for Multi-Skill Agent Optimization
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly use skills as a lightweight way to acquire task-specific knowledge. Recent work enables skills to evolve from task trajectories. However, these methods often lack systematic management of evolved skills, making it difficult for agents to reuse and accumulate skills across domains, thus limiting performance on subsequent tasks.To reliably accumulate, reuse, and maintain useful skills across tasks, we present SELM (Self-Evolving Library Management), a framework that formulates skill evolution as library-level management. SELM jointly manages skill retrieval, updating, and lifecycle by maintaining skill confidence and utility signals. It introduces utility-aware retrieval to select useful skills, a Map-Reduce framework to generate targeted updates from task-specific experience, and lifecycle controls to retain or remove skills based on their effectiveness. These mechanisms enable the skill library to continuously accumulate useful experience while preserving and pruning skills across tasks, improving agent performance on complex tasks across diverse domains. We evaluate SELM on four agent benchmarks covering diverse tasks and execution environments, and SELM consistently outperforms in most settings.

papers.title: Random Tournaments Are Asymptotically Almost Surely Link-irregular
papers.abstract: Bastien and Khormali (2025) conjectured that a nontrivial link-irregular tournament with $n$ vertices exists if and only if $n \ge 6$. Their work establishes the conjecture for $n \le 100$. We present a probabilistic argument for the existence of link-irregular tournaments with $n$ vertices when $n \ge 9$ to resolve the conjecture. In fact, we show that a random tournament is asymptotically almost surely link-irregular.

papers.title: One-loop mixing matrix of the N=1 SYM Supercurrent operator upon renormalization on the Lattice using stout-smeared Links
papers.abstract: We extend the perturbative investigation of the renormalization and mixing patterns of the supercurrent operator in lattice ${\cal N}=1$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills (SYM) theory, using stout-smeared gauge links. We employ the SLiNC action for gluinos and a family of Symanzik improved gauge actions for gluons. Building upon previous studies employing clover-improved fermions and the Wilson gauge action, we compute the one-loop mixing matrix of the supercurrent operator among gauge-invariant and gauge-variant operators. Particular emphasis is placed on the structure of operator mixing in the presence of stout smearing parameters. Our results contribute toward refining fine-tuning strategies necessary for the restoration of supersymmetry in the continuum limit, and provide a stepping stone for future perturbative and nonperturbative investigations in supersymmetric theories on the lattice.

papers.title: Theory of High-Temperature Fractional Chern Phases in Monolayer van der Waals Kagome Materials A$_2$T$_3$X$_4$
papers.abstract: Fractional Chern insulators bring the fractional quantum Hall effect, with its anyonic excitations, to zero magnetic field. So far they have been realized in moiré materials, where the long superlattice period weakens electronic interactions and confines these phases to cryogenic temperatures. Early proposals instead envisioned topological flat bands on atomic-scale lattices, where fractionalization could persist to far higher temperatures, but a suitable material has been lacking. Here we theoretically identify monolayers of the van der Waals kagome family $\mathrm{A}_2\mathrm{T}_3\mathrm{X}_4$ as such a platform, combining intrinsic topological flat bands and strong Coulomb interactions with gate-tunable carrier density and layer assembly. Exact diagonalization of models derived from density functional theory reveals ferromagnetism over broad filling ranges, supporting diverse fractional Chern insulators, anomalous composite Fermi liquids, and charge-ordered phases. In particular, in $\mathrm{Cs}_2\mathrm{Pd}_3\mathrm{S}_4$, the fractional Chern insulator exhibits a many-body gap of approximately 26 meV in the largest system accessible with band mixing allowing at most one interband electron-hole excitation. Layer assembly further provides a natural route to fractional quantum spin Hall insulators: bilayers with antiparallel magnetizations support this phase at realistic separations. These results identify an experimentally accessible material family in which chemical composition, carrier density, and stacking offer complementary routes to fractionalization at enhanced energy scales and control over topological order.

papers.title: ISR Reconstruction of Radiative $C=+1$ Charmonia as the Origin of the Belle--BESIII Line-Shape Puzzle
papers.abstract: A longstanding disagreement persists between Belle and BESIII over the line shapes of $e^+e^-\to Λ_c^+\barΛ_c^-$, $D_sD_{s1}(2536)$, and $D_sD_{s2}^{*}(2573)$ near 4.63 GeV. Belle observes enhancements through initial state radiation that are absent or much weaker at BESIII. We propose that the extra Belle yield arises from radiative production of a $C=+1$ charmonium. Luminosity normalization increases this contribution to the extracted cross sections, so tens of fb can explain the enhancements. Belle II can test this mechanism through full reconstruction and searches for missing charmonia in open charm modes.

papers.title: Sharp Wasserstein stability and small-delay thresholds for evolution equations with measure-valued principal-part delays
papers.abstract: We study the dependence of solutions to coercive evolution equations on the law of a measure-valued delay acting through the principal spatial operator. For non-negative delay measures of equal mass, transport couplings and the time-translation modulus of one reference trajectory yield quantitative kernel-stability estimates. Fractional temporal regularity gives a Wasserstein rate, with explicit glueing and data criteria for its application. For moving point delays in a diffusion model, a solution-level lower bound matches both the rate and its dependence on the kernel mass. This matching estimate holds for zero prescribed history and uniformly bounded forcing in the natural dual energy space. The results also quantify concentration to positive delays and approximation by atomic quadrature. Separately, we determine a sharp class-level threshold for energy bounds uniform in the delay location. At the critical threshold, any fixed scalar mode is spectrally stable, but uniform space--time energy control fails in a small-delay, high-frequency limit. Above the threshold, the growth has an explicit asymptotic logarithmic rate.

papers.title: The Yau Geometric Conjecture for Isolated Hypersurface Singularities
papers.abstract: This paper presents a proof of the long-standing Yau Geometric Conjecture.

papers.title: Turning Number and the Geometry of Disorder-Induced Topology
papers.abstract: The geometry of momentum-space Hamiltonian maps derived from the zero-frequency single-particle Green's function provides a route to a refined topological characterization of quantum systems beyond the noninteracting clean limit. The central idea is to complement standard topological invariants by invariants that characterize the geometry of the map itself. As a paradigmatic example, we study the one-dimensional chiral Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with disorder, where the topological Hamiltonian defines a planar Bloch loop. In addition to its conventional winding number, this loop possesses an integer turning number that characterizes the winding of its tangent vector. We identify turning-number transitions that occur while the topological Hamiltonian remains finite and spectrally gapped, driven solely by a vanishing tangent vector of the Bloch loop, and obtain an extended phase diagram with additional topological structure beyond the winding-number classification. Asymptotic analysis predicts the emergence and disorder dependence of the corresponding transition regime, in agreement with the numerical results. Our findings establish the geometry of momentum-space Hamiltonian maps as an additional source of topological structure beyond conventional classifications.

papers.title: Optimal degree bounds for sum-of-squares representations
papers.abstract: The moment-sum-of-squares (SOS) hierarchy provides a sequence of bounds on the minimum of a polynomial over a basic closed semialgebraic set, i.e., a subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ defined by finitely many polynomial constraints. We establish optimal bounds on the error of the SOS hierarchy in the following settings: 1. If the constraints define an Archimedean quadratic module: the error of the Putinar-based hierarchy at level $k$ is $Θ((\log k)^4/k^2)$ in the worst case. 2. If the constraints define a compact semialgebraic set: the error of the Schmüdgen-based hierarchy at level $k$ is $Θ((\log k)^2/k^2)$ in the worst case. 3. If the constraints define an Archimedean quadratic module and satisfy linear independence constraint qualification conditions (LICQ): the error of the hierarchy at level $k$ is $Θ(1/k^{4})$ in the worst case. Here, the upper bound holds already for the Putinar-based hierarchy, while the lower bound holds even against the Schmüdgen-based hierarchy. Equivalently, these give best-possible effective versions of Putinar's and Schmüdgen's Positivstellensätze for these settings (in terms of their dependence on $k$).

papers.title: Shear SAW piezoelectricity of single-crystalline $\mathrm{LiNbO_3}$ films grown on $42^{\circ}$ YX-$\mathrm{LiTaO_3}$ substrates by DLI-CVD
papers.abstract: Direct growth of single-crystalline $\mathrm{LiNbO_3}$ films with technologically relevant nonpolar orientations and a single ferroelectric domain state remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the epitaxial growth of a 320-nm-thick, single-domain $42°$ YX-oriented $\mathrm{LiNbO_3}$ film on a congruent $42°$ YX-cut $\mathrm{LiTaO_3}$ substrate by direct liquid injection chemical vapor deposition. The deposition temperature was limited to $600°\mathrm{C}$ to preserve the ferroelectric domain state of the $\mathrm{LiTaO_3}$ substrate. X-ray diffraction confirmed that the $\mathrm{LiNbO_3}$ film inherited the substrate orientation and domain state and exhibited no detectable secondary phases. The LN rocking-curve full width at half maximum was $0.011°$, approaching the instrumental resolution and demonstrating its high crystalline quality. Single-port leaky surface acoustic wave (LSAW) resonators with a wavelength of $4\,μ\mathrm{m}$ were fabricated on the $\mathrm{LiNbO_3/LiTaO_3}$ heterostructure and on a bare $\mathrm{LiTaO_3}$ reference substrate. At approximately 1 GHz, the $\mathrm{LiNbO_3/LiTaO_3}$-based resonators exhibited an electromechanical coupling coefficient of about 13%, compared to 8.5% for the reference $\mathrm{LiTaO_3}$-based resonators. These results demonstrate that direct epitaxial growth can produce high-quality, strongly piezoelectric $\mathrm{LiNbO_3}$ films and provide a route toward thickness-controlled layered substrates for high-performance acoustic devices.

papers.title: Say It or Grab It? Conversational Control of UI Adaptations in Mixed Reality
papers.abstract: Mixed reality interfaces must continuously adapt to a user's changing task and environment, yet adaptation policies are fixed in advance, either preset by the system or configured by the user. Natural language offers a way to state changing needs mid-task, but whether users can express interface behavior this way, and what it gains over direct manipulation, is unknown. We first elicited how users verbalize adaptation needs (N=19). We then built ConverseMR, which translates a spoken request into adaptation objectives and constraints and satisfies them continuously as the user's context changes. In a within-subjects study (N=24), conversational and direct control proved complementary: direct manipulation for precision, ConverseMR for reach and expressive breadth, with their combination rated highest. Spoken commands were rarely final and users frequently refined and replaced them upon experiencing the result, characteristic of, what we call, user-led adaptation, where users communicate adaption needs and the system identifies a solution.

papers.title: Widely Linear-Enhanced IQ Imbalance Interference Cancellation for AFDM-FTN Systems
papers.abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) networks require reliable and spectrally efficient wireless links to support massive device connectivity and high mobility applications. To meet these requirements, this paper investigates a widely linear (WL)-empowered receiver design for affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) with faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) signaling under practical receiver in phase and quadrature imbalance (IQI). The considered AFDM-FTN system couples the direct and image branches with FTN induced intersymbol interference (FTN-ISI) and delay-Doppler spreading in the affine domain. To address this coupled interference structure, a unified conjugate augmented input output model is established for IQI impaired AFDM-FTN systems. Based on this model, a WL minimum mean square error receiver with parallel interference cancellation (WL-MMSE-PIC) is developed, where WL-MMSE preprocessing is followed by the proposed hard decision PIC (HD-PIC) and damped soft decision PIC (SD-PIC). The proposed receiver is further analyzed in terms of the local stability of HD-PIC, a genie aided performance reference under ideal residual interference cancellation, and the impact of the AFDM chirp parameter on the post equalization interference distribution. Simulation results show that the proposed WL-MMSE-HD-PIC and WL-MMSE-SD-PIC receivers achieve significant error rate performance gains over the conventional linear-MMSE and WL-MMSE baselines. The results further show that FTN signaling provides a nominal spectral-efficiency gain, while residual-coupling-based chirp-parameter selection reduces the post-equalization residual coupling and improves detection reliability for high-mobility IoT links.
